sections.title: Power take-off

rows.label: Speed
rows.value: 540 rpm

rows.label: Drive
rows.value: Transmission-driven with single clutch; live with dual-stage clutch

sections.explainer: Power path: engine → flywheel → clutch → gearbox input → PTO drive shaft through the gearbox → PTO engagement coupler → rear PTO output shaft. With a single-stage clutch, pressing the pedal stops the PTO along with the wheels. With a dual-stage clutch, the first half of pedal travel releases only the gearbox drive, so the PTO keeps turning (live PTO). The full pedal releases both.

sections.title: Hydraulic lift

rows.label: System
rows.value: Ferguson System with draft control and position control (twin-lever quadrant)

rows.label: Pump
rows.value: Camshaft-driven piston pump with cam blocks and valve chamber(s); later pattern from serial 65685

rows.label: Pump drive
rows.value: Driven with the PTO drive line, so it stops with the clutch on single-clutch tractors

rows.label: Lift ram
rows.value: Single-acting ram in the lift cover; 3 in piston from serial 65685

sections.explainer: Lifting: the PTO drive line turns the pump camshaft. The pump pistons send oil through the control valve to the ram cylinder under the lift cover. The ram pushes the rockshaft round, and the lift arms pull up the lift rods and lower links. Draft control: when the soil pulls harder on the implement, the top link pushes on the main control spring, and that moves the control valve. The implement then lifts slightly, and it drops again when the load eases. Position control: the lever sets a height and the valve holds the lift arms there. (Summary to be checked against the service manual.)

steps.title: Find the serial plate
steps.text: On the dashboard / instrument console. Its exact position varies by model. Note the full letter prefix and the number.

steps.title: Read the prefix letters
steps.text: 1st letter is the chassis, 2nd is the fuel and 3rd is the clutch. For example, a D in second place means Standard diesel, and an M in third place means dual-stage clutch.

steps.title: Check the engine number
steps.text: Standard engines have no plate. On the diesel, the number is stamped into the block just above the dynamo on the right-hand side. A 3-cylinder engine is a later Perkins replacement.

steps.title: Check casting dates
steps.text: UK castings carry day/month/year codes. The centre housing code is on the right-hand side, forward of the round port.

steps.title: If the plate is missing
steps.text: The tractor serial was recorded only on the plate. Use casting dates and the engine number. Friends of Ferguson Heritage hold records of UK-built 35s.

steps.title: Test the clutch
steps.text: Engine running, gear in neutral, PTO engaged. Press the clutch slowly to about half travel. If the PTO or hydraulics keep working, it is the dual-stage clutch (live PTO).

identification.prefixNote: Letter meanings come from one supplier source, which says some letters apply only to UK-built tractors and some only to early MF tractors. They have not yet been checked against a known 1958 UK plate.
